That is: part of the condition of your following me is that, if you see something from me and you know that it is correct, but the wajh (reasoning) of its correctness is hidden from you, and you feel in yourself a disapproval, you should not open the matter with me by asking, nor reopen it with me, until I am the one who opens it to you. This is part of the adab (etiquette) of the student toward the scholar, and of the follower toward the one followed.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 71:

﴿So they set out until, when they boarded the ship, he made a hole in it.﴾ They set out along the sea shore, seeking a ship. When they boarded it, its people said, "They are thieves." The ship's owner said, "I see the faces of prophets." So they carried them without a fare. When they reached the deep water (lajjaju), al-Khidr took the axe (p-٣１٢) and made a hole in the ship by pulling out two planks from its boards on the side facing the water. Musa began stuffing the hole with his garments. Then ﴿he said, "Have you made a hole in it to drown its people?"﴾ "Li-yaghraqa ahluha" ("to drown its people") is read by Hamzah and Ali, from غَرِقَ (ghariqa, to drown). ﴿You have certainly done a terrible thing.﴾ "You have done a great thing," from أمِرَ الأمْرُ (amira al-amr, the matter became grave), when it grew great.

Translation of the passage:

﴿He said﴾ i.e., al-Khidr, ﴿"Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾

"When Moses saw that the hole was one the water would not enter, and he did not leave the ship, [Moses] said: ﴿Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot﴾ — either for 'that which I forgot,' or 'for something I forgot,' or 'for my forgetting.' He meant that he had forgotten his covenant [with you], and there is no blame upon people for forgetting. Or he meant by forgetting 'abandoning': i.e., do not hold me accountable for what I abandoned of your instruction the first time. ﴿And do not impose upon me difficulty in my affair﴾ — 'arhaqahu' means: when it overtakes him and 'arhaqahu iyyah' means to cover him with it. That is: do not overwhelm me with difficulty in my affair, which is following you. I.e., do not make my following you hard for me, but make it easy for me by overlooking and not pressing me with questions."

So they set off until, when they met a boy, he killed him. It was said: he struck his head against the wall. It was also said: he laid him down and then slaughtered him with a knife. As for why it says ﴿فَقَتَلَهُ﴾ ("then he killed him") with the particle *fa'* (then/so), while it says ﴿خَرَقَها﴾ ("he made a hole in it") without *fa'*: the making of the hole was made the response (*jaza'*, the consequent) of the conditional (*shart*), and the killing was placed within the protasis (*shart*, the condition) as something conjoined to it (*ma'tuf 'alayhi*), while the response is ﴿أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا﴾ ("Have you killed a soul?"). The two were treated differently because the making of the hole in the ship did not follow their boarding, whereas the killing did follow their meeting the boy.

﴿زَكِيَّةً﴾ (pure, innocent): the Hijazi reader and Abu 'Amr read "زاكِيَةً" (*zakiyah*). It means one who is free from sins. This is either because he (Khidr) regarded her as pure, since he had not seen her commit a sin, or because she was a child who had not reached the age of legal responsibility (*hinth*).

﴿بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ﴾ (without a soul, i.e., not in retaliation for a life): meaning she had not killed a soul, so that retaliation (*qisas*) could be exacted from her. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that Najdah al-Haruri (the Kharijite) wrote to him asking how it was permissible to kill him, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden the killing of children. He wrote back to him: "If you know of the circumstances of the children what the knowing one (Khidr) of Moses knew, then you may kill them."

﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا نُكْرًا﴾ (You have certainly done a dreadful thing): the word *nukran* is read with the *kaf* vowelled with a *damma* (*nukr*) by the Medinan reader (Nafi') and Abu Bakr, and the meaning is *al-munkar* (the reprehensible). It was said: *nukr* is less than *imr* (the grave, the enormity), because killing one soul is easier than drowning the people of the ship. Or its meaning is: "You have done a thing more reprehensible than the first, because a hole can be repaired by patching it, whereas killing cannot be repaired."

He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?" (﴿قالَ ألَمْ أقُلْ لَكَ إنَّكَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبْرًا﴾) He added "لَكَ" (to you) here, because the disapproval (al-nukr) in it is greater.

Translation:

﴿He said, "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep company with me; you will have received an excuse from me."﴾ "After this" means after this time or this question. ﴿Do not keep company with me﴾ ... ﴿You have received an excuse from me﴾ means: you have made me without excuse in what lies between me and you regarding parting. And "ladunni" with the nun lightened is read by Madani and Abu Bakr.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 77:

﴿So they set out, until when they came to the people of a town⦅qarya⦆﴾ It was Antioch, or Ayla, and it is the farthest land of Allah from the sky. ﴿They asked its people for food⦆ (istad'ama) ⦅meaning⦆ they asked them for hospitality (istadafa). ﴿But they refused to receive them as guests⦆ (yudayyifuhuma). Dayyafahu means: he lodged him and made him his guest. The Prophet ﷺ said: "They were a people of town who were lowly and miserly (li'am)." It is also said: the worst of towns is the one that is stingy with hospitality. ﴿Then they found in it⦆ in the town ﴿a wall⦆ whose height was one hundred cubits ﴿about to collapse⦆, that is, about to fall. The word "will" (iradah) is used metaphorically for approaching and being on the verge, just as "concern" (hamm) and "resolve" (azm) are used for that. ﴿So he set it up⦆ with his hand, or he wiped it with his hand so it stood upright and straightened; or he tore it down and rebuilt it. The situation was one of necessity and need for food, and need had gripped them to the last resource of a person, which is asking. They found no one to console them. When he (Khidr) had set up the wall, Musa could not contain himself, because of what he saw of deprivation and the touch of need, and ﴿said: "If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it."⦆ That is: you could have sought a payment for your work, so that you could ward off the necessity with it.

"Latta-khadhta" with the tā' lightened, the kasra on the khā', and the dhāl assimilated (idgham): Basrī reading. With the dhāl clearly pronounced: Makkī reading. With the tā' doubled, the fatha on the khā', and the dhāl clearly pronounced: Ḥafṣ reading. With the tā' doubled, the fatha on the khā', and the dhāl assimilated into the tā': the others. The tā' in takhadha is a root letter, as in tabi'a, and ittakhadha (iftaʿala) derived from it is like ittaba'a from tabi'a; it has nothing to do with al-akhdh (taking).

﴿He said: "This is the parting between me and you."﴾ "This" refers to the third question. That is, this objection is the cause of the parting. The original wording would be "This is a parting between me and you," and it has also been read that way. The verbal noun (maṣdar, the noun denoting the action) is then annexed to the adverbial complement (ẓarf, the noun of time or place), just as it is annexed to the direct object. ﴿I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 79:

﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor men who worked on the sea.﴾ It is said: it belonged to ten brothers, five of whom were disabled (zamnā) and five of whom worked on the sea. ﴿So I wished to damage it.﴾ I made it defective. ﴿And behind them was a king﴾ — in front of them, or behind them; their route on their return was past him. What they did not know of his situation, God informed al-Khidr of; and he was a Jalandā (a tyrant, Jalandā). ﴿who seizes every boat by force﴾ — that is, he seizes every boat that is sound and free of defect by force, and if it is defective he leaves it. "Ghaṣban" (by force) is either a verbal noun (maṣdar) or an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu). If you say: his saying "so I wished to damage it" is caused by the fear of the seizure of the boat, so its proper order would be to come after the cause — I say: the intended meaning is the delay, but it was placed first for emphasis (li-l-ʿināya).

Verse 80: "As for the boy, his name was al-Husayn, and his parents were believers, so We feared lest he should overburden them with rebellion and disbelief."

"So We feared" (فَخِفْنا): We feared that he would overwhelm the two believing parents with "rebellion" (طُغْيانًا) against them and "disbelief" (وكُفْرًا) in their blessing, by his disobedience and his evil conduct; and that he would bring upon them evil and affliction, or pass on to them his disease, or lead them astray by his misguidance so that they would apostatize because of him. This is from the words of al-Khidr. Al-Khidr feared this from him only because Allah, exalted is He, informed him of his condition and made him aware of the secret of his affair. And if it is from the words of Allah, exalted is He, then the meaning of "fa-khashīnā" (فَخَشِينا, "so We feared") is "fa-'alimnā" (فَعَلِمْنا, "so We knew"): if he lived, he would become a cause of disbelief for his parents.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 81:

﴿So We intended that their Lord should replace them﴾ "yubaddilahumā rabbuhumā" (that their Lord replace them) is read by Madani and Abu 'Amr. ﴿with one better than him in purity﴾ — in purity (ṭahāra) and cleanliness (naqā') from sins. ﴿and nearer in mercy﴾ — in compassion (raḥma) and tenderness (ʿaṭf). "Zakāatan" and "ruḥman" are accusatives of specification (tamyīz). It is narrated that a female slave was born to them, whom a prophet married, and she bore a prophet; or that He replaced them with a believing son like them. "Ruḥuman" is read by Shami, and both are dialectal variants (lughatān).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 82:

﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys﴾ Asram and Sarim, ﴿in the city﴾ — it is the village mentioned earlier. ﴿Beneath it was a treasure belonging to them﴾ — that is, a tablet of gold on which was written: "I marvel at one who believes in destiny, how he grieves; I marvel at one who believes in provision, how he toils; I marvel at one who believes in death, how he rejoices; I marvel at one who believes in reckoning, how he is heedless; I marvel at one who knows the world and its turning over its people, how he feels secure in it. There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Or it was buried wealth of gold and silver, or pages containing knowledge. The first view is the most apparent. It is related from Qatadah: the treasure was made lawful for those before us and made unlawful for us, and spoils of war were made unlawful for them and made lawful for us. ﴿Their father was righteous﴾ — it was said that he was their seventh grandfather. ﴿Among those who keep company with me.﴾ It is related from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said to one of the Kharijites in a discussion that took place between them: "By what did Allah preserve the two boys?" He said: "By the righteousness of their father." He said: "Then my father and my grandfather are better than him." ﴿So your Lord desired that they reach their maturity (ashudd-huma)﴾ — that is, the age of puberty ﴿and extract their treasure as a mercy﴾ — it is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), or a verbal noun in the accusative governed by "your Lord desired," since it carries the meaning of "had mercy on them." ﴿From your Lord. And I did not do it﴾ — I did not do what you saw ﴿on my own command﴾ — by my own ijtihad. Rather, I did it by the command of Allah. The pronoun may refer to everything, or to the wall. ﴿That﴾ — that is, the three answers ﴿is the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾ — the ta' has been dropped for lightness (in ta-sti'). Some people's feet have slipped into misguidance by preferring the saint (wali) over the Prophet, and this is manifest disbelief, since they said: Moses was commanded to learn from al-Khadir, who is a saint. The answer: al-Khadir was a prophet, even if some claim otherwise. This was a trial for Moses, peace be upon him. Moreover, the People of the Book say that this Moses is not Moses son of 'Imran, but Moses son of Manan. It is impossible for a saint to be a saint unless he believes in the Prophet, and then the Prophet should be lower than the saint. There is no shame in Moses seeking knowledge, because increase in knowledge is desirable. Mention was made first of "fa-aradtu" because it is corruption in outward appearance, and it is his own act; third, "fa-arada rabbuka," because it is pure bounty and beyond human capacity; and second, "fa-aradna," because it is corruption in terms of the act and bounty in terms of the change. al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "fa-aradna" is "then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, desired," and similar to it in the Qur'an there are many instances.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 83:

﴿They ask you﴾, that is, the Jews, as a test, or Abu Jahl and his followers, ﴿about Dhu al-Qarnayn (the Two-Horned One)﴾. He is Alexander (al-Iskandar), who ruled the world. It was said that two believers ruled the world, Dhu al-Qarnayn and Sulayman, and two disbelievers, Nimrod and Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), and Nimrod came before him. It was also said that he was a righteous servant whom Allah made king over the earth, gave knowledge and wisdom, and subjected to him light and darkness, so that when he travelled, the light guided him from in front of him and darkness surrounded him from behind. It was also said that he was a prophet, and it was said that he was one of the angels. It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "He was neither an angel nor a prophet, but he was a righteous servant. He was struck on his right horn in obedience to Allah and died. Then Allah raised him up, and he was struck on his left horn and died, and Allah raised him up. Thus he was named Dhu al-Qarnayn. And among you there is one like him," meaning himself. It was said that he used to call them to tawhid (the affirmation of Allah's oneness), and they would kill him, and Allah would bring him back to life. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He was named Dhu al-Qarnayn because he travelled to the two horns of the world," meaning its two sides, east and west. It was also said that he had two horns, that is, two braids, or that two generations of people passed away in his time. Or it was because he ruled the Romans and the Persians, or the Turks and the Romans. Or there were two horns on his crown, or on his head was something resembling two horns. Or he was noble on both sides, from his father and his mother, and he was from the Romans.

﴿Say: I will recite to you from him﴾, from Dhu al-Qarnayn, ﴿a mention﴾.

"Indeed, We established him firmly in the land" ﴿إنّا مَكَّنّا لَهُ في الأرْضِ﴾: We made for him a station and eminence therein.

﴿وَآتَيْناهُ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ "And We gave him of every thing" — of whatever he desired of his aims and objectives in his kingdom, ﴿سَبَبًا﴾ "a means" [al-Kahf 18:85] — a way leading him to it.

**﴿So he followed a means﴾**. The sabab (means, a route by which one reaches the goal) is that by which one attains the intended aim, whether by knowledge or by power. He wished to reach the west, so he followed a means that brought him to it, until he reached it. Likewise he wished to reach the east, so he followed a means, and he wished to reach the two barriers, so he followed a means. "Fa-atba'a" and "thumma atba'a" are read by Kufans and Syrians (with the alif of the verb cut, i.e., as *atba'a*). The rest read them with the alif joined and the ta' doubled (*fa-ittaba'a*).

From al-Asma'i: *atba'a* means "to catch up with," and *ittaba'a* means "to follow and track," even if one does not catch up.

﴿Until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun﴾: that is, the furthest point of inhabited land toward the west. Likewise the rising-place. He (ﷺ) said: "The beginning of his affair was that he found in the books that one of the sons of Sam drinks from the Spring of Life and so becomes immortal. So he began to travel in search of it, with al-Khadir as his minister and his maternal cousin. He found it and drank from it, but Dhu al-Qarnayn did not find it."

﴿He found it setting in a spring of black mud﴾: that is, full of mud (ḥam'ah), from the phrase ḥamiʾat al-bi'r, "the well became full of mud." The reading "ḥāmiyah" (burning, hot) is by Ibn 'Amir, Ibn Kathir's Kufan companions, and others, except Hafs, and it means "hot." It is also reported that Abu Dhar said: "I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a camel. He saw the sun as it set and said: 'Do you know, Abu Dhar, where this sets?' I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It sets in a hot spring.'"

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) was with Mu'awiyah, and Mu'awiyah recited "ḥāmiyah," whereupon Ibn 'Abbas said "ḥamiʾah." Mu'awiyah then asked 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar: "How do you recite it?" He replied: "As the Commander of the Faithful recites it." Then Mu'awiyah turned to Ka'b al-Ahbar and asked: "How do you find the sun setting?" He said: "In water and mud. So we find it in the Tawrah (Torah)." This agreed with the statement of Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both). There is no contradiction, so it is possible that the spring combines both descriptions together.

﴿And he found near it﴾: near that spring, ﴿a people﴾ who were naked of clothing; their clothing was the hides of game, and their food was what the sea cast up. They were disbelievers.

﴿We said: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them or you take a kindly course with them."﴾ If he was a prophet, then Allah revealed this to him. Otherwise it was revealed to a prophet, who then commanded him with it. Or it was inspiration (ilhām), and he was given the choice between punishing them by killing them if they persisted in their affair, or taking a kindly course with them by honoring them and teaching them the laws if they believed. "Punishment" means killing, and "taking a kindly course" means taking them captive, because compared with killing, it is a kindness. (p-318)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 87:

﴿He said﴾ Dhu al-Qarnayn, ﴿As for him who does wrong, we will punish him﴾ with killing, ﴿then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾ in the Hereafter. That is: as for him whom I called to Islam but who refused anything other than persisting in the great wrong, which is shirk (association of partners with God), he is the one punished in both abodes.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 88:

﴿And as for him who believes and does righteous deeds﴾ That is: he does what faith requires. ﴿For him is a reward, the good (al-husna)﴾ That is, for him is the reward of the good deed, which is the word of testimony (kalimat al-shahada). The reading "jaza'an al-husna" (as "reward, the good") is that of the Kufans other than Abu Bakr; that is, for him is the good deed as a reward. ﴿And We shall speak to him of Our command with ease﴾ That is: having ease; that is, We shall not command him with what is difficult and burdensome, but with what is easy and manageable, such as zakat, kharaj, and other things.

Until, when he reached the rising-place of the sun, he found it rising upon a people (﴿حَتّى إذا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ الشَمْسِ وجَدَها تَطْلُعُ عَلى قَوْمٍ﴾), and they were the Zanj (black people) (﴿وهُمُ الزِنْجُ﴾), ﴿for whom We had made no shelter from it (the sun)﴾ (﴿لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهم مِن دُونِها﴾), that is, apart from the sun, ﴿any screen﴾ (﴿سِتْرًا﴾), meaning: buildings on the open land of their country, which do not hold up buildings, and in which there are caves. When the sun rises they enter them, and when the day has risen high they go out to their livelihoods. Or "the screen" means clothing. From Mujahid: those among the Sudan who do not wear clothes at the rising of the sun are more numerous than all the people of the earth.

**﴿Thus⦆** — that is, the matter of Dhul-Qarnayn is thus, i.e., as We have described it, glorifying his affair. **﴿And We had full knowledge of what was with him⦈** — of the armies, the equipment, and the means of kingship. **﴿Khubran⦈** — an accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar), because in *aḥatnā* there is the meaning of *khabarnā* (We had knowledge of). Or: he reached the rising place of the sun in the same manner, i.e., just as he reached its setting place; or: it rises upon a people similar to that tribe upon whom it sets, meaning: they are disbelievers like them, and their judgment is like their judgment in his punishing whoever among them remained upon disbelief and his kindness toward whoever among them believed. (p-319)

﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾: between the two mountains. They were two mountains that Dhu al-Qarnayn sealed off, closing the gap between them. The reading "al-saddayn" (with a fatha on the sin) and "saddan" is transmitted by Makki (Ibn Kathir), Abu 'Amr and Hafs. The reading "al-sudayn" (with a damma on the sin) and "sudan" is transmitted by Hamzah and Ali (al-Kisa'i). Others read both with a damma. It is said that what was blocked by creation itself takes the damma, while what was blocked by the work of people takes the fatha.

"Bayn" (between) is in the accusative because it is the object (maf'ul bihi) of "balagha" (reached). It is in the genitive through annexation in ﴿This is the parting between me and you﴾ [al-Kahf: 78], and in the nominative in ﴿Indeed your relations have been severed among you﴾ [al-An'am: 94]. This is because it is one of the adverbs (zuruf) that are used both as nouns and as adverbs. This place lies at the farthest edge of the land of the Turks on the side facing the east.

﴿He found beside them﴾: that is, behind them, ﴿a people﴾, who were the Turks, ﴿who scarcely understood any speech﴾: that is, they could barely understand it except with great effort and difficulty, through gestures and the like. "Yufqihuna" (they make understood) is read by Hamzah and Ali, meaning they do not make the listener understand their speech or explain it, because their language is strange and unknown.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 94:**

﴿They said: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, indeed Ya'juj and Ma'juj are corrupters in the land."﴾ They are two foreign names (*a'jamiyyan*), as shown by their being non-declinable (*man' al-sarf*, the grammatical prohibition of nunation and certain case endings). Ásim alone read their initial hamza (*hamzahuma*). They are from the progeny of Yafith (Japheth), or Ya'juj is from the Turks and Ma'juj is from the Jil and the Daylam.

﴿Corrupters in the land.﴾ It was said that they used to eat people. It was also said that they would go out in the spring, leaving nothing green without eating it or anything dry without carrying it away. None of them would die until he saw a thousand male offspring from his own loins, all of whom had taken up arms. It was also said that they were of two kinds: tall ones of extreme height, and short ones of extreme shortness.

﴿Shall we then assign for you a tribute (*kharjan*)?﴾ Hamza and Ali read it as *kharajan* (with a fatha on the ra' and an alif after it), meaning a reward (*ju'lan*) that we would bring out from our wealth. Its counterpart is *al-nawl* and *al-nawal*.

﴿On condition that you place between us and them a barrier (*saddan*).﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 95:

﴿He said: "That in which my Lord has established me is better"﴾ — with idgham (assimilation) and with its unassimilated reading, makkani (both forms are read). ﴿In it my Lord is better﴾, i.e., what He has granted me of firm establishment (makin) through abundance of wealth and ease is "better" than what you offer me of (p-320) kharaj (tribute), so I have no need of it. ﴿So help me with strength﴾ — with workmen and craftsmen who excel at building and labour, and with tools. ﴿I will set between you and them a barrier (radm)﴾ — a wall, or a firm, strong, well-secured barrier. And the radm is greater than the sadd.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 96:

﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾ — pieces of iron. The zubra (sing. of zubar) is a large piece. It is said: he dug the foundation until he reached water, and made the foundation of rock and molten copper, and the building of blocks of iron, with wood and charcoal between them, until he filled the space between the two mountains up to their tops. Then he placed the bellows, until it became like fire, and poured the molten copper over the heated iron, so it mixed and its parts stuck to one another and it became a solid mountain. It is also said that the distance between the two barriers was a hundred farsakh.

﴿Until, when he had levelled between the two cliffs﴾ — with two fathahs (ṣadafayn), the two sides of the two mountains, because they face each other (yatasadaqān), i.e., they stand opposite each other. Makki, Basri and Shami read "al-ṣudufayn," while Abu Bakr reads "al-ṣudfayn."

﴿He said: Blow﴾ — i.e., Dhu al-Qarnayn said to the workers: blow into the iron.

﴿Until, when he had made it﴾ — i.e., the thing blown upon, which is the iron — ﴿fire﴾, like fire.

﴿He said: Bring me﴾ — give me. ﴿That I may pour over it molten copper﴾ — molten copper, because it drips (yaqtur). It is in the accusative governed by "afrigh" (pour), and its underlying structure is: "Bring me copper; pour over it copper," so the first was omitted because the second indicates it.

"Qala ituni" (with a wasl alif) is read by Hamza; when beginning, he pronounces the alif with a kasra, i.e., "jī'ūnī" (come to me).

﴿So they were not able﴾ with the tā' dropped for lightness, because the tā' (ت) is close in its place of articulation to the ṭā' (ط). ﴿to scale it﴾: that is, to climb over the barrier. ﴿Nor could they find a way through it﴾: that is, they had no means of climbing it, because of its height, nor of piercing it, because of its hardness.

"He said: This is a mercy from my Lord." That is: this barrier is a blessing from Allah and a mercy upon His servants; or, this empowerment and enabling to construct it (is a mercy from my Lord). ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes﴾: that is, when the coming of the Day of Resurrection draws near and is about to arrive, ﴿He will make it level⁠﴾ — that is, the barrier — "dakkan" — meaning leveled, flattened, made even with the ground. Anything that spreads out after having been raised has become "indakka." "Dakkaa'" (in the reading of Kufan scholars) means level ground, i.e., a flat land. ﴿And the promise of my Lord is ever true﴾ — this is the last statement of Dhu al-Qarnayn.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 99:**

﴿And We shall leave﴾, meaning and We shall make, ﴿some of them﴾, meaning some of the creation, ﴿on that Day surging﴾, meaning mixing, ﴿upon one another﴾. That is, they will be agitated and will mingle, both mankind and jinn, bewildered. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and that they will surge when they emerge from behind the barrier, crowding into the lands. It is narrated that they will come to the sea and drink its water and eat its creatures, then eat the trees and whoever of the people they overcome, and they will not be able to reach Makkah, Madinah, and Bayt al-Maqdis. Then Allah will send a worm (naghaf) into their necks, which will enter their ears, and they will die. ﴿And the Horn is blown﴾ for the establishment of the Hour, ﴿and We shall gather them﴾, that is, the creation will be gathered for reward and punishment, ﴿a gathering﴾, an emphasis.
And We shall present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, presenting it plainly (ʿarḍan). And We displayed it to them, so they saw it and beheld it.

﴿Those whose eyes were under a covering from My remembrance﴾: from My signs, which are looked at; or from the Qur'an, so that they would mention it with glorification; or from the Qur'an and reflection on its meanings. ﴿And they could not bear to hear﴾: that is, they were deaf to it. However, this is more emphatic, since a deaf person may be able to hear when he is shouted at, whereas these people are as if their hearing had been struck deaf, so they have no capacity to hear. (p-322)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 102:

﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants instead of Me as protectors?﴾ That is: Do the disbelievers suppose that their taking as protectors My servants—meaning the angels and ʿIsā, peace be upon them—will benefit them? Evil is what they supposed. It has been said that "an" (that) together with its complement stands in place of the two objects of "afa-ḥasiba" (do they think), and "ʿibādī awliyāʾ" (My servants as protectors) are the two objects of "an yattakhidhū" (that they take); and this is the more likely (awjah) view, meaning that they will not be protectors for them. ﴿Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a nuzul﴾. The nuzul is what is prepared for a guest upon arrival, namely the guest's provision and the like. ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾

﴿Say: Shall We inform you of those who lose the most in their deeds?﴾ أعمالًا is a tamyiz (specification, an accusative noun clarifying what the preceding word refers to). It was put in the plural, whereas the analogical expectation (qiyas) is that it should be singular, because of the diversity of their desires (li-tanawwu' al-ahwa'). They are the People of the Book, or the monks.

﴿Those whose effort has gone astray﴾: it was lost and came to nothing. The word ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ (alladhina) is in the nominative case (*fi mahalli'l-raf'*, في مَحَلِّ الرَفْعِ). That is, the meaning is: they are those who ﴿in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing good work﴾.

﴿Those are they who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds are void, and We shall not assign them any weight on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ So they will have no weight or value with Us.

Here is the translation:

﴿That is their recompense: Hell﴾ — "Hell" is an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) to "their recompense." ﴿Because they disbelieved and took My signs and My messengers in mockery﴾. That is: their recompense is Hell because of their disbelief and their mockery of the signs of God and His messengers.

Eternally abiding therein (﴿خالِدِينَ فِيها﴾) is a circumstantial clause (حال). ﴿They shall not desire any removal from it﴾ (﴿لا يَبْغُونَ عَنْها حِوَلا﴾): ḥiwal means a transition (تَحَوُّلًا) to something other than it, being content with what they have been given. It is said: ḥāla min makānihi ḥiwalan, meaning he moved from his place; i.e., there is no addition beyond it, such that their souls would strive toward something more complete for their aims and wishes. Or this is the ultimate of the description, because a person in this world, in whatever bliss he may be, is aspiring, with his gaze inclined toward something higher than it. Or the intended meaning is the negation of any transition and the emphasis of eternity (khulūd).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 109:

﴿Say: Even if the sea were ink for the words of my Lord﴾ — i.e., the water of the sea. Abu 'Ubayda said: al-midad (ink) is that with which one writes; i.e., even if the words of God's knowledge and wisdom were written down, and the sea were ink for them. The word "sea" here is meant generically. ﴿The sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it﴾ — the like of the sea — ﴿as a supplement (madadan)﴾ — it would also be exhausted. The words are not exhaustible. "Madadan" is a specifying accusative (tamyiz), as in "I have the like of him, a man." Al-madad is like al-midad, that by which something is supplied. "Tanfad" (will be exhausted) is read by Hamza and Ali. It is also said that Huyayy ibn Akhtab said: "In your Book is: ﴿And whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good﴾ [al-Baqara: 269]; then you recite: ﴿And you have not been given of knowledge except a little﴾ [al-Isra: 85]." So this was revealed, meaning: that wisdom is indeed a great good, but it is a drop from the sea of the words of God.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 110:

﴿Say: I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾ — then whoever hopes to attain the good of meeting his Lord, and to meet Him in a meeting of pleasure and acceptance; or whoever fears the evil of meeting his Lord. What is meant by "meeting" is coming before Him (al-qudum), and it has been said that it means seeing Him, as is the literal sense of the word; and the hope, on this view, remains upon its literal meaning. ﴿Let him do righteous work﴾, sincere, not intending by it anything but the Face of his Lord, and not mixing with it anything else. It is reported from Yahya ibn Mu'adh that it is "what one would not be ashamed of [before people]." ﴿And let him not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾: this is a prohibition of shirk (associating partners with God) or of riya' (showing off). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the minor shirk." They said: "What is the minor shirk?" He said: "Riya' (showing off)."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf is protected for eight days from every trial that occurs. If the Dajjal (Antichrist) emerges within those eight days, Allah will protect him from the trial of the Dajjal. And whoever recites ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me﴾ up to its end when lying down to sleep, there will be for him a light shining from his bed to Makkah, filled with that light are angels who send blessings upon him until he rises from his bed. And if his bed is in Makkah and he recites it, there will be for him a light shining from his bed to the Bayt al-Ma'mur, filled with that light are angels who send blessings upon him and seek forgiveness for him until he wakes up."
